regions.label: Map O.3 — Combining satellite imagery with household survey data increases the resolution of the poverty map of Tanzania
regions.summary: Two 2018 Tanzania poverty-incidence maps compare a Household Budget Survey map for 20 regions with a finer map combining that survey data and satellite imagery for 169 districts.
regions.details: The figure has two side-by-side panels. (a) “Poverty map using the Household Budget Survey (20 regions)” shows regional boundaries and names. Its legend is “Poverty incidence, 2018 (% of population)”: 36–45, 32–35, 26–31, 22–25, 8–21, and No data. It also marks the national capital, international boundaries, and province boundaries. (b) “Poverty map combining the data in panel a with satellite imagery (169 districts)” shows finer district boundaries. Its legend uses the same measure and year, with classes 38–67, 31–37, 24–30, 17–23, 4–16, and No data; it also marks the national capital, international boundaries, and district boundaries. Both maps depict Tanzania, including mainland and Zanzibar; Dodoma is marked as the national capital. Source: World Bank 2019; data link printed as http://bit.do/WDR2021-Map-O_3. Map identifier printed near the lower right: IBRD TAN45642 | MARCH 2021.
regions.limitations: The maps encode ranges by color; individual locations do not have printed numeric incidence values. Some small district shapes and labels are difficult to distinguish at this page scale. The panels use different poverty-class intervals, so the color categories are not identical.
